4. The learned Assistant Judge, 5th Additional Court, Dhaka by his judgment and decree dated 9-4-2000 decreed the suit in-part. 

 5. The defendant-petitioner, thereafter, preferred Title Appeal No. 284 of 2000 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka against the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 9-4-2000 which was subsequently transferred to the Court of Paribesh Appeal Adalat, Dhaka for disposal. 

 8. The plaintiff-opposite party resisted the said report dated 7-7-2002 by filing written objection contending inter alia that the Advocate Commissioner by suppressing the real fact submitted a report as per desire of the defendant No. 1 stating that there is no existence of road in the suit property although the judgment and decree dated 19-6-1999 passed in Title Suit No. 230 of 1997 and Heba-Bil-Ewaz deed No. 333 dated 9-1-1983 clearly suggests about the existence of the road/path in question and, as such, the Advocate commissioner's report dated 7-7-2002 is liable to be rejected. 

 12. Mr Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party, on the other hand, sup-ports the impugned order dated 9-10-2004 which according to him just was correct and proper. He submits that the Advocate Commissioner's report is not only false but also contrary to the clear findings on the point of road or passage given in the judgment and decree dated 29-6-1999 passed in Title Suit No. 230 of 1997 and in that view of the matter the Court of appeal below rightly refused to accept the Advocate Commissioner's report on the clear finding that it was incorrect. Finally, the learned Advocate submits that in the facts and circumstances of the case if according to the impugned order dated 9-10-2004 any further local investigation is held that will not cause prejudice to any of the parties in any way whatsoever, rather that will be the best option for both the parties.
